segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And calling his twelve disciples to him, he gave them authority over unclean spirits, to drive them out and to heal every disease and every illness.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: These are the names of the twelve apostles: first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax collector; James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Simon the Cananaean, and Judas Iscariot, the one who also handed him over.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: These twelve Jesus sent out with these instructions:

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Do not go off down any road to the Gentiles, and do not enter any town of the Samaritans;

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: but go instead to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: As you go, proclaim, ‘The kingdom of the heavens has come near.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse those with skin disease, drive out demons. You received without payment; give without payment.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Do not acquire gold or silver or copper for your belts,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: nor a bag for the road, nor two tunics, nor sandals, nor a staff; for the worker is worthy of his food.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Whatever town or village you enter, find out who in it is worthy, and stay there until you leave.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: As you enter the house, greet it.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If the house is worthy, let your peace come upon it; but if it is not worthy, let your peace return to you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And if anyone will not welcome you or listen to your words, shake the dust off your feet as you leave that house or town.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Truly I tell you, it will be more bearable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that town.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Look, I am sending you out like sheep among wolves; so be as shrewd as snakes and as innocent as doves.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Be on your guard against people, for they will hand you over to councils and flog you in their synagogues,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and you will be brought before governors and kings on my account, as a testimony to them and to the Gentiles.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But when they hand you over, do not worry about how you are to speak or what you are to say; for what you are to say will be given to you in that hour.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For it is not you who are speaking, but the Spirit of your Father speaking in you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Brother will hand over brother to death, and a father his child; children will rise up against parents and have them put to death.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You will be hated by everyone because of my name. But whoever endures to the end will be saved.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: When they persecute you in one town, flee to the next; for truly I tell you, you will certainly not finish going through the towns of Israel before the Son of Man comes.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: A disciple is not above the teacher, nor a slave above his master.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: It is enough for the disciple to become like his teacher, and the slave like his master. If they have called the head of the house Beelzebul, how much more the members of his household!

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: So do not fear them; for nothing is covered that will not be uncovered, and nothing hidden that will not be made known.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: What I tell you in the dark, say in the light; and what you hear in your ear, proclaim on the housetops.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Fear instead the one who can destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Are not two sparrows sold for a penny? Yet not one of them will fall to the ground apart from your Father.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: As for you, even the hairs of your head are all numbered.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: So do not fear; you are worth more than many sparrows.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: So everyone who acknowledges me before people, I also will acknowledge before my Father who is in the heavens;

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: but whoever denies me before people, I also will deny before my Father who is in the heavens.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Do not think that I came to bring peace on the earth. I did not come to bring peace, but a sword.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For I came to turn a man against his father, and a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law;

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and a person’s enemies will be the members of their own household.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Whoever loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me, and whoever loves son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me;

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and whoever does not take up their cross and follow after me is not worthy of me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Whoever finds their life will lose it, and whoever loses their life on my account will find it.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Whoever welcomes you welcomes me, and whoever welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Whoever welcomes a prophet as a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward, and whoever welcomes a righteous person as a righteous person will receive a righteous person’s reward.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And whoever gives one of these little ones even a cup of cold water as a disciple—truly I tell you, that person will certainly not lose their reward.”

notes.traditional: the Canaanite; the Cananaean; the Zealot
notes.note: The byname transliterates an Aramaic word meaning “zealous one”; it has nothing to do with Canaan or the village of Cana. Luke’s list gives the Greek equivalent, “the Zealot”. Whether it marks religious zeal in general or a link with a militant movement is disputed.

The Greek verb is the ordinary word for handing a person into someone else’s custody, and the same word is used in verses 17, 19 and 21 for what will happen to the disciples. Most English versions say “betrayed” when Judas is the subject, which names the treachery the story supplies but hides the repetition. Some scholars defend “betray” as a legitimate contextual sense here.

One Greek word means both “nations” and, in the plural from a Jewish standpoint, the non-Jewish peoples; it is rendered “Gentiles” or “nations” according to sense. The phrase is literally “a road of Gentiles”, most likely a road leading into Gentile territory. This mission is limited to Israel; the Gospel’s closing scene sends the disciples to all the nations.

The Greek is plural, reflecting a Hebrew and Aramaic way of speaking that a first-century hearer would have noticed. Most translations flatten it to “heaven”. The phrase is Matthew’s usual equivalent of “the kingdom of God”.

The word names people with the scaly skin conditions regulated in Leviticus 13–14, which made a person ritually unclean; that is why they are “cleansed” and not simply healed. “Leper” today means someone with Hansen’s disease, which is narrower than the Greek term and may not even be included in it. Most translations keep “lepers” with a footnote, partly because “skin disease” can understate the social exclusion involved.

notes.phrase: let your peace come upon it
notes.note: The ordinary Jewish greeting on entering a house was a wish of peace, so “greet it” in verse 12 means to speak peace over the household. The saying treats that spoken peace as a real blessing that either rests on the house or returns to the one who gave it.

notes.phrase: before the Son of Man comes
notes.note: What “coming” is meant is disputed. Proposals include Jesus’ vindication in his resurrection and exaltation, the destruction of Jerusalem in 70 CE, and his final coming, with the mission to Israel continuing until then. The Greek does not settle the question.
The Greek word means a person owned by a master, not a hired servant. Many English versions soften it to “servant”; some recent ones use “slave”, as here.

A name for the ruler of the demons, as the accusation later in this Gospel makes explicit. Its origin is uncertain; many scholars think it means something like “lord of the dwelling”, which would make a pun with “head of the house”. Older English versions have “Beelzebub”, following the Latin.

Gehenna is a place name, the Valley of Hinnom outside Jerusalem, which had become the name for the place of final judgment. “Hell” merges it with Hades and with later imagery, so the name is kept. Many translations still use “hell”, usually with a footnote giving Gehenna.
The coin is an assarion, a small copper coin worth one-sixteenth of a denarius, the denarius being roughly a day’s wage for a laborer. “Penny” stands for a coin of very little value.
The Greek says only “without your Father”. Translations often supply “without your Father’s will”, “knowledge” or “care”; the Greek does not choose among them, and the rendering leaves it open.

notes.phrase: to turn a man against his father
notes.note: Verses 35–36 echo Micah 7:6, where the breakdown of trust within the family is a sign of a time of crisis. Jesus applies the prophet’s words to the division his own mission will cause.

The Greek word here is the same one rendered “soul” in verse 28. It most often means a person’s life or living self; “soul” is used in verse 28 because there it is set against the body as what killing cannot reach. All major translations divide the word between “life” and “soul” by context.

notes.traditional: in the name of a prophet
notes.note: The Greek is literally “into the name of a prophet”, an idiom meaning “on the ground that he is a prophet”. The literal phrase suggests to an English reader that someone’s name is being invoked, so the sense is given instead; several modern versions do the same. In verse 42 “as a disciple” likewise means that the little one is given the drink because he is a disciple.

candidates.reason: Versions divide between “servant”, “slave” and “bondservant”, and the word recurs across the Gospels, Paul and Revelation, including as a self-designation of the apostles.
For exorcisms translators vary between “cast out”, “drive out” and “expel”, and the phrase recurs constantly in the Synoptics and Acts.
“Receive” and “welcome” are both common for the reception of people and of the message, and the sayings in verses 40–42 have parallels in other Gospels that should match.
“Confess”, “acknowledge” and “declare” all appear in translations, and “confess” now suggests admitting guilt; the word recurs in John, Romans, Hebrews and 1 John.
“Be anxious”, “worry” and “be concerned” compete across Matthew 6, Luke 12, 1 Corinthians 7 and Philippians, and readers should see that it is the same word.
